messages:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: SERVICE=INFERENCE-GATEWAY severity=high — error_rate (5xx) > 3% over 3m. Incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD123456 :rotating_light:
Emily S: Acked. I'm oncall for this shift — taking ownership. @Rajiv can you pull traces for the last 10m?
Rajiv: Looking now. I see a correlated spike in 502s across eu-west1 and us-west2. Traces show repeated KV cache timeouts hitting the gateway sidecars.
Lina: Also seeing increased connection queueing on the ingress LB around 00:09-00:12 UTC. CPU on gateway pod nodes is fine, but sidecar p99 latency jumps.
Emily S: Noted. @deploy-bot any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: model-serving v2.5-canary -> 00:08:13 UTC on cluster inference-prod. (canary: 5%)
Kira: That timing aligns. Customers on routes pinned to the canary show higher error rates. Early hypothesis: canary is producing responses that cause KV lookups to spike (long tail).
Rajiv: Agreed. Suggest disabling the canary and switching traffic to stable immediately. If that doesn't help, scale up gateway pool and enable fallback model routing.
Emily S: Doing a safe disable now. Running:
```
# disable canary
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-router CANARY_ENABLED=false --record
# scale ingress
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/gateway-ingress --replicas=6
```
Emily S: Command ran — canary env toggled, gateway scaled to 6 pods.
Tom (support): I'll prep a status blurb for status.redwood.ai and ping CS to flag customers in the impacted cohorts. :writing_hand:
Rajiv: Pulling logs from one of the affected sidecars, snippet:
```
[2026-02-14T00:10:02Z] kvcache: timeout after 250ms fetching prefix=usr:session:abc123
[2026-02-14T00:10:02Z] gateway: upstream error: 502 Bad Gateway — kv_fetch_fail
```
Rajiv: Looks like KV store latency spike + canary load pattern. Might be cascade from a new model generating heavier context keys.
Kira: Customer impact summary: about 3% of total requests in the 00:08-00:14 UTC window returned 5xx. Top affected customers are two mid-market tenants (IDs hidden) — volume low but sensitive. No major SLA breaches reported yet, but worth follow-up.
Emily S: Monitoring metrics now — error rate dropping to 0.9% over the last 4m after the disable/scale. Chart: https://grafana.example/d/abc/error-rate?panelId=2
incidents-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD123456 acknowledged by Emily S at 00:15:09 UTC.
Lina: I rebalanced KV traffic and increased the cache client timeouts temporarily to avoid thrashing. Applied:
```
# temp config tweak
redis.client.timeout=500ms
redis.client.maxRetries=3
```
Lina: Rebalanced looks promising, p95 kvcache latency down from 380ms -> 45ms.
Tom (support): Status update drafted and scheduled. Sharing with @Kira for review before publish.
Kira: Reviewed, minor wording tweak and go-ahead. Posting now.
Rajiv: Error rate steady ~0.6% for the last 6m. No new spike windows in the traces. Root cause candidate: canary model produced denser KV access patterns causing eviction storms.
Emily S: Handoff: I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and handing to daytime SRE rotation at 07:00 UTC. Follow-up action items: 1) revert canary fully, 2) run KV warmup for heavy prefix patterns, 3) add canary traffic limits and circuit breaker for kvcache.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout v2.5-canary -> rollback complete at 00:20:45 UTC (traffic 100% -> stable).
Emily S: Thanks all — I'll keep the thread open for 20m and close if stable. :white_check_mark:
Lina: Filed post-incident ticket INFRA-789 with logs and diagnostic steps.
Rajiv: Will do a deeper RCA tomorrow and propose a quantized canary profile.
Emily S: Closing note: no immediate customer escalations, CS notified, monitoring alerts adjusted. If error rate creeps back up, we re-open PD.
incidents-bot: Incident PD123456 closed automatically by Emily S at 00:34:40 UTC.
